description: Declarative rebrand map applied by rebrand/transform.py to an extracted pegasus package tree before it is repackaged as DARQ. No engine source or content is copied into this repo; this file only describes a transform applied at build time to a downloaded, pinned release artifact.
renames_notes: This list is NOT exhaustive and must not be treated as one: it holds only the deliberate, non-mechanical re-namings -- paths whose target isn't a textual substitution of the source (the 'king-pegasus' persona becomes 'arquitecto-darq', not a string swap of 'pegasus'). Every other branded content path -- including ones the engine adds later, such as agents/pegasus-general.md -- is renamed mechanically by rebrand/transform.py::rename_relative_path, which runs the path through the same substitution map applied to file bodies (masking protected tokens the same way). The former 'agents/pegasus-orchestrator.md' and 'agents/mcp/cbm@pegasus-orchestrator.md' entries were removed from this list after verifying byte-for-byte that mechanical derivation reproduces their exact former targets (see tests/test_rebrand.py). A transform-time mirror check fails loudly, naming the offending path, if any resolved path -- explicit or derived -- still carries the brand.
forbidden_fragments_notes: Declares WHAT COUNTS AS a brand leak in a resolved output path, as distinct from 'substitutions', which declares HOW a leak already found is repaired. These are deliberately different registers with different purposes and must never be merged into one list: a fragment can belong here without ever being a rewrite rule (e.g. 'harness' is not a substitution key -- no rule turns 'harness' into anything -- but a path still carrying it is still a leak), and a rewrite rule's left-hand side (e.g. 'king-pegasus') is also, by construction, a fragment that must never survive resolution. rebrand/transform.py's mirror check reads the UNION of this list and every substitution key so it can catch a leak regardless of which register names it.
substitution_notes: Order is correctness-critical: each rule is applied to the whole tree, in this exact order, before the next rule runs. Longest / most specific patterns come first so 'king-pegasus' becomes 'arquitecto-darq' as a whole before the bare 'pegasus' rule could ever turn it into the wrong 'king-darq'. Applied only to '.md' and '.txt' files; every other file extension is left untouched.
protected_tokens_notes: Stable wire identifiers that must stay byte-identical across every distribution (schema strings, env var names, journal/report keys, data-dir prefixes). Masked out before any substitution rule runs and restored verbatim afterward, so no substitution -- however broad -- can ever touch them. Masking (and later unmasking) walks this list longest-first, so a token that is itself a prefix of another protected token (e.g. '.pegasus-' inside '.pegasus-data') never clips the longer one out from under it. `tools/verify_darq.py`'s leak scan treats every one of these as SILENT by design.
excluded_paths_notes: content/__init__.py is never read or rewritten by the transform, regardless of extension rules.

accepted_residue.reason: npm package name baked into notifier/package.json and its package-lock.json. JSON files are excluded from body substitution entirely by design (see substitution_notes), and renaming it here would desync the lockfile's recorded package identity from what npm actually resolved at publish time. Upstream work in Pegasus.

Installed system-prompt artifact filename, referenced verbatim from opencode.json's instructions list. The journal tracks it by this exact id; renaming it here without an upstream rename would break instruction loading. Upstream work in Pegasus.

Subtree path of the skill-registry static asset tree (shell wrapper + Python module). Renaming a whole directory of engine-authored scripts, and every internal path reference between them, is upstream work in Pegasus, not something DARQ's per-file rebrand can safely do.
Executable name of the skill-registry tool, referenced from its own shell wrapper, from the plugin that shells out to it, and from the generated .env contract. Upstream work in Pegasus.
The skill-registry tool's own module filename, referenced by its shell wrapper. Same upstream constraint as the executable name above.
Config file generated by the plugin at install time, named after the skill-registry executable it points at. Same upstream constraint as the executable name above.

Prose and UI mentions of the tool's display name: comments in pegasus_skill_registry.py and plugins/pegasus-skill-registry.ts, and that plugin's own notification toast title. The toast title is genuinely user-visible, not just invisible plumbing -- called out here rather than folded silently into the filename residue above.
Self-referential docstring inside pegasus_skill_registry.py describing its own purpose.
Static asset filename shipped as-is; the rebrand transform only rewrites '.md' and '.txt' file bodies (see substitution_notes), so a '.ts' asset's own filename is never touched.
Exported symbol name inside that same static .ts asset. Same substitution-scope limitation as the filename above.
Static asset filename, same substitution-scope limitation as plugins/pegasus-orchestrator-notifier.ts.
Exported symbol name inside that static .ts asset. Same substitution-scope limitation as its filename.
Static asset filename, same substitution-scope limitation as the other two plugin assets.
Exported symbol name inside that static .ts asset. Same substitution-scope limitation as its filename.

Config/cache directory name (~/.config/pegasus-zellij-state, ~/.cache/pegasus-zellij-state) hardcoded inside the same static .ts asset alongside its exported symbol. Same substitution-scope limitation: '.ts' assets are never rewritten.

Synthesized npm root package name the engine embeds in mcp/playwright-package-lock.json at content-load time; pegasus/core/content.py::_require_lockfile_pins requires the lockfile's root 'name' to match exactly what a synthesized package.json reuses verbatim, so rewriting it here would desync the lockfile from what content-load-time validation expects. JSON files are excluded from body substitution entirely by design. Not exercised by a plain 'darq install --cli opencode' (the Playwright MCP is a separate opt-in); kept from the original inventory but unverified against v5.19.0's default install path.

accepted_residue_notes: Cosmetic, deferred upstream debt: branded names DARQ ships as-is because they are journal-tracked artifact ids or static engine assets outside the rebrand transform's reach. Reported as a NOTE on a clean run; never fails the check. Every entry must carry both 'token' and a non-empty 'reason' -- tools/verify_darq.py fails loudly at load time if either is missing.
known_defects_notes: Functional defects that survive rebranding, kept separate from cosmetic accepted_residue on purpose: mixing the two once let a live offender hide as an intentional exemption behind a false stated reason. Reported as a WARNING (loud, on every run) rather than silently or as a NOTE; never fails the check because it is a known, accepted-for-now state rather than a new regression. Every entry must carry both 'token' and a non-empty 'reason', enforced the same way as accepted_residue.
